stories.headline: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition filed against CM Vijay’s victory from Perambur
stories.title: Madras High Court refuses to reject election petition filed against CM Vijay’s victory from Perambur
stories.summary: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan dismisses an application filed by the Chief Minister to reject the election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Madras High Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) refused to reject an election petition filed against the victory of Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay from the Perambur Assembly constituency, which he had retained after winning from two constituencies and resigning from the Tiruchi East seat.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan dismissed an application filed by the Chief Minister to reject the election petition filed by a voter, S. Dinesh, at the threshold, without forcing him to undergo the long-drawn process of facing a full-fledged trial to disprove the charges levelled against him by the election petitioner.

The judge said, the election petitioner had made out a cause of action for the conduct of a trial and that the veracity of the allegations levelled by him against the Chief Minister could be decided only after appreciating the evidence to be produced during the course of the trial.
What did the election plea say?
The election petition, filed through advocate V.R. Shanmuganathan, had accused the Chief Minister of having suppressed various facts related to his properties in the election affidavit.

The petitioner alleged that the Chief Minister had claimed ownership over 50 cents of government poromboke land at Vilpatti village in Kodaikanal, falsely declared a property sold by him for ₹35 crore at Padi in Chennai as his property worth ₹7 crore, and wrongly termed his Neelangarai bungalow as inherited property.

The petitioner had insisted that the election of the Chief Minister must be declared null and void for “wilful and deliberate” suppression, misrepresentation, and false declarations with respect to many of the immovable properties referred to in his 2026 election affidavit.
He said, Mr. Vijay had claimed to have purchased the Vilpatti agricultural land for a consideration of ₹30,000 in 1997 and that the present market value of the property was around ₹20 lakh.
However, an examination of the village ‘A’ register revealed that the property was actually a government poromboke land, the litigant said.
Similarly, the Chief Minister had declared to have purchased a non-agricultural land measuring 33,955 square feet at Porur in Chennai for a consideration of ₹9.13 crore in 2010.
However, an examination of Registration Department documents revealed that he had purchased only 20,773 square feet for ₹7.5 crore.
There was no explanation for the excess declaration of the extent of the land as well as the sale amount, the petitioner added.

stories.headline: Andhra Pradesh: 280 employees skip election duty in Krishna, get show cause notices
stories.title: Andhra Pradesh: 280 employees skip election duty in Krishna, get show cause notices
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Krishna district election authority in Andhra Pradesh has issued show-cause notices to 280 employees who failed to report for election duty during the local body polls on November 26.
They have been asked to submit explanations with supporting evidence by 6 pm on November 27.

District Election Officer and Collector DK Balaji said on Thursday, November 26, that 74 employees assigned to municipal election duties and 206 assigned to gram panchayat polls were absent without prior permission.
Among the 74 municipal employees, 16 were presiding officers, 12 assistant presiding officers, and 46 other polling officers.
Gudivada municipality accounted for 45 absentees, including 11 presiding officers, five assistant presiding officers, and 29 other polling officers.
In Tadigadapa municipality, 29 employees were absent, comprising five presiding officers, seven assistant presiding officers, and 17 other polling officers.
The 206 employees who failed to report for the first phase of gram panchayat elections included 119 presiding officers and 87 other polling officers.
Gannavaram had the highest number of absentees at 62, followed by Unguturu with 42, Gudivada with 39, Bapulapadu with 29, Gudlavalleru with 24, and Nandivada with 10.
Balaji said the employees were required to report at their designated distribution centres on November 25 to collect election material before proceeding to their allotted polling stations.
Those who fail to provide satisfactory explanations and supporting evidence will face disciplinary action.
The notices come as the first phase of gram panchayat elections in six mandals of Krishna district recorded a voter turnout of 79.77% on November 26.
Of the 2,63,603 registered voters, 2,10,270 cast their votes.

stories.headline: Infra push, anti-doping steps highlighted by India in meet with IOC Future Host panel
stories.title: Infra push, anti-doping steps highlighted by India in meet with IOC Future Host panel
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 26: Highlighting the rapid development of sports infrastructure in the country and "aggressive anti-doping measures" in the last couple of years, India presented its roadmap for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online interaction with the International Olympic Committee's Future Host Commission here on Thursday. The 30-minute presentation on Ahmedabad's preparedness was spearheaded by outgoing Indian Olympic Association President P T Usha and its CEO Raghuram Iyer. This was followed by a brief discussion with the Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic-led nine-member Future Host Commission. According to a reliable source, the exchange after the presentation lasted about 20 minutes during which the Commission members posed queries related to India's planned budget, the measures that would be taken to ensure sustainability of venues, issues related to "clean sports", athlete experience and how the Games would help the Olympic movement in the country. "The entire Commission joined the online presentation from various parts of the world. The exchange was positive. Apart from highlighting the infrastructure push, we also spoke about the tough anti-doping measures being taken to curb the use of prohibited substances," the source told PTI. "The Commission was keen to know about the sustainability measures that will be taken to ensure that the venues don't lie dormant after the Games. They were satisfied with the way India responded and the general sentiment towards our vision was positive," the source added. India has significantly scaled up testing and is also working towards criminalising doping through legislation that would introduce jail terms and hefty fines on those involved in supplying banned substances to athletes. Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, who attended Thursday's meet at the Sports Authority of India headquarters here, has asserted repeatedly that doping would be addressed at a war footing. India has been topping the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of most violators among major nations for the last three years. In a press release issued after the meeting, the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) said the presentation covered proposed host city Ahmedabad's preparedness. "It also covered India's experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans, and the long-term vision for delivering the Games," stated the IOA. "I mean it's still very early days. There is a long way to go and lots of preparations to be done," said IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer after the meeting, referring to the three stages of dialogue that will follow the current Continuous Dialogue phase of the bidding process.

stories.headline: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
stories.title: India-US trade deal close to completion: Goyal amid fresh tariff threat
stories.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal is nearing completion, with the process and roadmap for finalising the pact, which had earlier held up negotiations, now taking shape. "The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape," Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually. The remarks came after the latest US Trade Representative's (USTR) report proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.

stories.headline: GCC cries foul over heavy machinery deployment on Pissu Top–Shri Amarnath Ji shrine stretch
stories.title: GCC cries foul over heavy machinery deployment on Pissu Top–Shri Amarnath Ji shrine stretch
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 26: The Group of Concerned Citizens (GCC) has expressed concern over the grave ecological and environmental consequences of using heavy machinery for road construction in the Sheshnag and Baltal areas along the route to the Shri Amarnath Ji shrine. The Group has urged Lieutenant Governor Shri Manoj Sinha to ensure that geotechnical, hydrological and environmental impact assessments are conducted before any further activity on these road projects. In a memorandum submitted to the Lieutenant Governor on Tuesday, the Group recalled the frequent landslides and tunnel construction activities in recent years across several parts of the Himalayan region, including Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Jammu & Kashmir, caused by excessive and indiscriminate construction activity in environmentally sensitive areas. “The environmentally and ecologically fragile stretches from Pissu Top to the Amarnath Ji shrine (on the Pahalgam side) and from Baltal to the Amarnath Ji shrine (on the Sonamarg side) form part of either the Overa-Aru and Thajwas Wildlife Sanctuaries or their eco-sensitive zones. The entire track belt lies at an altitude of 11,000 to 14,500 feet (at Mahagunas Pass), surrounded by mountain peaks and glaciers at an altitude of 15,000 feet. The high influx of radiation, anthropogenic activity and construction disturbances are likely to escalate disaster risks due to frequent and intense precipitation caused by climate change, along with geological triggers such as earthquakes in the area.” The GCC also stressed the importance of pre-construction geotechnical, hydrological and environmental impact assessments, warning that disasters such as glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), like those witnessed in Nepal, could strike without warning. The memorandum stated that such disasters had claimed over 1,500 lives, with 5,600 people reported missing. “Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and clearance from the Wildlife Boards (Central and UT) are prerequisites under the Environment Protection Act and the Indian Wildlife Act, respectively. The government must make it public whether the necessary pre-construction studies were undertaken and clearances obtained.” The memorandum also referred to the Supreme Court taking suo motu cognisance in Writ Petition (Civil) No. 284 of 2012 of the high number of pilgrim deaths, with 67 fatalities reported during the first 17 days of the 2012 Amarnath Yatra. The Hon'ble Court issued directions to improve facilities for pilgrims, including widening of walking tracks, while prohibiting metalled roads and heavy construction. It also issued directions regarding the protection of glaciers, water bodies and forests, proper waste management and sanitation, assessment of carrying capacity and regulation of crowds. The memorandum further recalled that in 2022, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) passed certain orders in the aftermath of flash floods during the Yatra, directing that riverbeds and floodplains near the shrine be kept free from encroachments, including the pitching of tents, to ensure that these areas performed their natural ecological functions and helped prevent catastrophic flash floods and casualties. “Sheshnag Lake is an oligotrophic alpine lake fed by snowmelt and surrounding glaciers. If continued human and machine activity close to the Sheshnag ecosystem and the overhanging glaciers triggers a GLOF, it could cause devastation downstream in Chandanwari, Pahalgam and surrounding villages on both banks of the Lidder River, extending all the way to Anantnag town and even beyond. Moreover, such construction activity close to glaciers will irreversibly endanger the long-term sustainability of these glaciers and Sheshnag Lake, thereby affecting the discharge in the Lidder River. This, in turn, will have very serious consequences for drinking water supplies and irrigation systems and, in fact, for the very survival of a huge population, numbering in lakhs, living downstream.” The Group has made a fervent appeal to the Lieutenant Governor to order an immediate halt to road construction activities and the use of heavy machinery/JCBs along the environmentally fragile, high-altitude routes to the Shri Amarnath Ji shrine from Pahalgam-Chandanwari and Baltal-Sonamarg.

stories.headline: India-US trade pact and tariffs: An explainer
stories.title: India-US trade pact and tariffs: An explainer
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 27: India and the US finalised the framework for the first phase of their bilateral trade agreement (BTA) in February this year, following negotiations that were launched in February 2025. But changes in Washington's tariff structure have brought the two sides back to the negotiating table. The US has proposed a fresh set of tariffs on 14 economies, including India. Here is an explainer to understand the developments so far. Why this trade pact? India is pursuing the agreement to safeguard the competitiveness of its exports amid high American tariffs and secure an edge over rival South and South East Asian manufacturing economies. Why these tariffs? The US is using tariffs against its trading partners such as India to address trade deficits, shield domestic industries from foreign competition and press countries to negotiate trade agreements on terms favourable to Washington. The US has alleged that trading partners like India and China impose steep import duties and restrictive regulations on American goods while enjoying low-tariff access to the US market. What is a tariff? It is a customs or import duty imposed by the importing country on goods entering its territory and paid by the importer. Tariffs increase the cost of imported goods and can make them more expensive than domestically produced products. They are used to protect domestic industries, generate government revenue and influence trade flows. Why US market important for India? The US has been India's largest trading partner since 2021-22. Exports grew 0.92 pc to USD 87.3 billion during 2025-26, while imports increased 15.95 per cent to USD 52.9 billion. India's trade surplus with the US declined to USD 34.4 billion in 2025-26 from USD 40.89 billion in 2024-25. The US is India's largest export destination for sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and electronics. Any increase in tariffs could affect the price competitiveness of Indian products and exporters' ability to retain or expand their market share. Why tariff landscape in US changing? The US announced a 25 pc duty from August 7, 2025. An additional 25 pc tariff was imposed on Indian goods as a penalty for New Delhi's continued purchase of Russian oil. After this order, the total tariff on Indian goods, barring an exemption list, rose to 50 pc. On February 2, 2026, India and the US agreed on a trade deal, under which Washington agreed to bring down the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 pc. On February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariff system. The Donald Trump administration subsequently turned to Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the US to impose tariffs following investigations into alleged unfair trade practices. The probes into forced labour and excess manufacturing capacity are part of Washington's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime under an alternative legal provision. On July 24, the US imposed a 10 and 12.5 pc tariff on 60 countries, including India (10 pc), under Section 301, citing concerns related to 'forced labour'. What triggered the latest development? The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods. For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement. US allegations on India? The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms. The report has identified sectors such as steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology as areas of concern. India's response? India has rejected the allegations, stating that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector. It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations. It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026. Joint statement? The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade. The terms of that pact include: - India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products. - The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement. - Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade. Important: "In the event of any changes to the agreed-upon tariffs of either country, the US and India agree that the other country may modify its commitments." - India intends to purchase USD 500 billion of US energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products, and coking coal over the next 5 years. \ Current status of talks? India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations. Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market. Has India received the advantage ? The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised. It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate). Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc. However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries. This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market. Experts view While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand. What next The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.

India is pursuing the agreement to safeguard the competitiveness of its exports amid high American tariffs and secure an edge over rival South and South East Asian manufacturing economies.
Why these tariffs?

The US is using tariffs against its trading partners such as India to address trade deficits, shield domestic industries from foreign competition and press countries to negotiate trade agreements on terms favourable to Washington.
The US has alleged that trading partners like India and China impose steep import duties and restrictive regulations on American goods while enjoying low-tariff access to the US market.
What is a tariff?
It is a customs or import duty imposed by the importing country on goods entering its territory and paid by the importer.
Tariffs increase the cost of imported goods and can make them more expensive than domestically produced products.
They are used to protect domestic industries, generate government revenue and influence trade flows.

The US has been India's largest trading partner since 2021-22.
Exports grew 0.92 pc to USD 87.3 billion during 2025-26, while imports increased 15.95 per cent to USD 52.9 billion.
The US is India's largest export destination for sectors such as textiles, pharmaceuticals, engineering goods, gems and jewellery, chemicals and electronics.
Any increase in tariffs could affect the price competitiveness of Indian products and exporters' ability to retain or expand their market share.
Why tariff landscape in US changing?
The US announced a 25 pc duty from August 7, 2025.
An additional 25 pc tariff was imposed on Indian goods as a penalty for New Delhi's continued purchase of Russian oil.
After this order, the total tariff on Indian goods, barring an exemption list, rose to 50 pc.
On February 2, 2026, India and the US agreed on a trade deal, under which Washington agreed to bring down the reciprocal tariff on Indian goods to 18 pc.
On February 20, the US Supreme Court struck down the reciprocal tariff system.
The Donald Trump administration subsequently turned to Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, which allows the US to impose tariffs following investigations into alleged unfair trade practices.
The probes into forced labour and excess manufacturing capacity are part of Washington's efforts to rebuild its tariff regime under an alternative legal provision.
On July 24, the US imposed a 10 and 12.5 pc tariff on 60 countries, including India (10 pc), under Section 301, citing concerns related to 'forced labour'.
What triggered the latest development?

The US Trade Representative (USTR) on November 25 announced the findings of its second Sec 301 investigations into structural excess manufacturing capacity in 14 economies, including India, and proposed additional tariffs on their goods.
For India, it proposed tariffs of up to 25 per cent, while indicating that the rate could be adjusted to 17 per cent if the two countries reach a trade agreement.
US allegations on India?

The USTR has alleged that India's industrial policies (such as the 'Make in India' initiative and PLI schemes), manufacturing expansion plans, labour protections, financial practices and market access barriers contribute to structural excess capacity and hurt American firms.
The report has identified sectors such as steel, solar, pharmaceuticals, medical devices and information and communications technology as areas of concern.
India's response?
India has rejected the allegations, stating that it does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.
It emphasised that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of the trade pact negotiations.
It said India remains committed to working closely with the US towards the early conclusion of the India-US BTA in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.
Joint statement?
The two countries announced that they have reached a framework for an interim agreement regarding reciprocal and mutually beneficial trade.
The terms of that pact include: - India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all US industrial goods and a wide range of food and agri products.
- The US will apply a reciprocal tariff rate of 18 pc on Indian goods, subject to the successful conclusion of the interim agreement.
- Both will address non-tariff barriers that affect bilateral trade.

Important: "In the event of any changes to the agreed-upon tariffs of either country, the US and India agree that the other country may modify its commitments." - India intends to purchase USD 500 billion of US energy products, aircraft and aircraft parts, precious metals, technology products, and coking coal over the next 5 years.
\ Current status of talks?
India has stated on multiple occasions that the deal has been finalised and will be signed once the US tariff framework is in place and India gets a comparative advantage over its competitor nations.

Comparative advantage means securing lower US import tariffs and better market access than rival manufacturing countries, such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, and China, so Indian exporters can price goods more competitively in the US market.
Has India received the advantage?
The latest USTR's report has proposed a 17 per cent tariff on India if the trade pact is finalised.
It gives only one per cent edge over Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Thailand (18 per cent deal rate) and a 3 per cent edge over Vietnam and China (20 per cent deal rate).
Without a pact, tariffs against India could go up to 25 pc.

However, according to experts, Indian exporters could face a tariff disadvantage against goods from several other countries in the US market, as Washington's latest Section 301 investigation into structural excess capacity covers only 14 trading partners, while the probe into forced-labour-related trade practices covers 60 countries.

This leaves a much larger group of economies (including Pakistan, Sri Lanka, the Philippines and Turkiye) potentially outside the additional tariff action, giving their exporters a relative cost advantage in the US market.
Experts view.

While exporters are urging the government to finalise the pact at the earliest, think tank GTRI said that with the threat of up to 100 pc Graham tariffs still looming, New Delhi must reject a one-sided trade deal and defend its industrial expansion sector by sector as serving legitimate domestic, export, and future demand.

The USTR has decided to schedule public hearings on its proposals on January 25 and has sought written comments from interested persons by January 5 as part of the final regulatory requirements before the tariffs come into effect.

stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
stories.title: Supreme Court refuses urgent listing of plea against Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana
stories.summary: A Bench headed by CJI Surya Kant said anyone with a different view of the epic is free to make a film of their own, as the film is already running in theatres
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) declined to list for urgent hearing a petition challenging the release of the Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, saying anyone with a different view of the epic was free to make a film of their own.
A Bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana observed that the film was already running in theatres, and that those who wanted to watch it had already done so.
The petitioner’s counsel told the Court that the plea had been registered on November 23, 2026, and was yet to be listed for hearing.
“The movie has already been released.
Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it,” the CJI said.
When the counsel argued that “many facts have been distorted” in the film, Justice Bagchi said, “They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand.
Don’t waste the time of the court.
If you have a counter view about the epic, make a movie based on that.” As the lawyer pressed for an early hearing, the Bench said the matter would be listed in due course.
The petition alleges that the makers distorted mythological facts in their depiction of the epic.
Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra.
It brings the epic to the big screen with Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.
The ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
stories.title: Supreme Court Appreciates Sucheta Dalal's PIL On Unclaimed Financial Assets, Disposes Plea Noting Measures Taken By Authorities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday disposed of a Public Interest Litigation filed by financial journalist Sucheta Dalal seeking directions to authorities to put in place measures enabling legal heirs to trace and claim unclaimed financial assets, including bank deposits, shares and mutual fund investments.

Noting that the Union Government, the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India have taken various administrative and regulatory steps to address the issue, the bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice R Mahadevan observed that judicial directions in that regard are not necessary.
At the same time, the bench placed on record its appreciation for Dalal for taking up a genuine public cause, saying that the case was an example of a responsible use of public interest litigation.
The bench also appreciated Advocate Prashant Bhushan for espousing the petitioners' cause with "passion and perseverance."

"The present proceedings were instituted not for securing any personal benefit but with the objective of protecting the financial interests of countless depositors, investors and their lawful claimants.
The petitioner has consistently drawn attention to the difficulties faced by ordinary citizens in identifying and recovering the unclaimed financial assets.
The concerns raised were genuine and the pursuit of the appropriate institutional measures to address them reflects a responsible exercise of public interest litigation," the bench observed.
However, the Court noted that the principal concerns raised have been substantially addressed by measures undertaken by the respondents (SEBI, RBI and the Department of Economic Affairs).

"We take on record the statements and assurances made in the respondents affidavits and expect the concerned authorities to continue the efforts towards improving the accessibility, efficiency, and transparency of the mechanism for identifying and recovering unclaimed financial assets.
No useful purpose will be served by keeping the petition pending for further monitoring of the regulatory measures already undertaken.
Any specific grievances concerning unclaimed financial assets may be pursued before the competent authority in accordance with law," the bench added.
The bench had reserved judgment on November 17.

stories.headline: Central University of Kashmir celebrates Constitution Day
stories.title: Central University of Kashmir celebrates Constitution Day
stories.summary: Ganderbal, Nov 26: The Department of Law, School of Legal Studies (SLS), Central University of Kashmir (CUK), celebrated Constitution Day-2026 under the theme “Hamara Samvidhan-Hamara Swabhiman” at the Tulmulla campus here on Thursday. The programme commemorated the adoption of the Constitution of India and reaffirmed the University's commitment to constitutional values and the principles enshrined in the founding document. In his keynote address (online), former Judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, Hon'ble Justice Paramjit Singh Dhaliwal, deliberated extensively on the concept of constitutionalism and the evolution of the basic structure doctrine, describing them as essential safeguards for preserving the constitutional framework. Drawing upon his extensive experience in the legal profession, he shared insights into the relationship between the Constitution, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary. He observed that constitutionalism was reflected not merely in judicial pronouncements but also in the conduct of citizens and public institutions, particularly in their commitment to upholding the rule of law. He elaborated on the historical evolution of the relationship between Parliament and the judiciary concerning the power to amend the Constitution, tracing important judicial developments from the early constitutional cases to the landmark Kesavananda Bharati judgment of 1973. Justice Dhaliwal also reflected upon the warnings articulated by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar in his concluding address to the Constituent Assembly, particularly against unconstitutional methods in politics and the absence of social democracy. He urged law students to develop independent thinking, engage critically with constitutional questions and support their arguments with reason and sound legal understanding. He emphasised that the true strength of constitutional democracy depended not only upon the institutions established under the Constitution but also upon the integrity, awareness and conduct of those who served and upheld it. Earlier, in his welcome address, Dean, School of Legal Studies, Prof. Farooq Ahmad Mir, emphasised that Constitution Day was not merely a ceremonial occasion but an opportunity to reflect upon the responsibilities that the Constitution places upon every citizen. Highlighting the significance of engaging students in the process of social transformation, he observed that meaningful change in society could be achieved only when students, teachers and families collectively became instruments of positive change. Referring to the Preamble, he underscored that the Constitution belongs to every citizen, irrespective of caste, creed, religion, region or language. He highlighted its commitment to securing social, economic and political justice, liberty of thought and expression, equality of status and opportunity, and fraternity, assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the nation. Tracing the making of the Constitution, Prof. Mir observed that it was the outcome of immense intellectual effort, deliberations and the sacrifices associated with India's freedom struggle. He noted that the Constituent Assembly took two years, eleven months and eighteen days to complete the historic task, with its members engaging in extensive discussions and deliberations before giving the country its Constitution. He further observed that the Constitution was a dynamic document whose relevance continued to be strengthened through judicial interpretation in response to the changing needs of society. The programme proceedings were conducted by Assistant Professor Dr. Gulafroz Jan, who also read the Preamble to the Constitution, with participants reaffirming their commitment to its ideals. Associate Professor Dr. Jehirul Islam proposed the vote of thanks. The Constitution Day Preamble reading and pledge-taking exercise were also organised across all campuses of the University. Meanwhile, the Directorate of Students Welfare also organised a debate competition as part of the Constitution Day celebrations.

stories.headline: Vikramaditya Singh seeks expert scrutiny over construction near Sheshnag
stories.title: Vikramaditya Singh seeks expert scrutiny over construction near Sheshnag
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 26: Former MLC of Congress, Vikramaditya Singh, has raised concerns over Border Roads Organisation (BRO) construction near Sheshnag Lake, warning that unchecked activity could cause irreversible damage to the fragile glacial ecosystem. Vikramaditya is grandson of Maharaja Hari Singh, the last Dogra ruler of Jammu and Kashmir, and son of former Sadr-e-Riyasat Dr Karan Singh. “The felling and burning of protected Chinar and Chestnut trees in Kashmir, along with BRO road construction in close proximity to the sacred Sheshnag Lake, are deeply concerning developments,” he said. “The experiences of Uttarakhand and Nepal serve as stark reminders of the consequences of unchecked / over-development and environmental neglect. The fragile ecosystem of Jammu & Kashmir, already under considerable stress, cannot afford such irreversible damage.” “It is our collective duty to preserve the natural beauty and unique ecology of Jammu & Kashmir for future generations.” “I urge the J&K Government and the concerned authorities to take serious cognisance of these activities and ensure strict monitoring before it is too late,” Singh wrote on X. He was responding to a post by environmental activist and Jammu and Kashmir Climate Action Group chairman Dr Raja Muzaffar Bhat, who sought an expert assessment of excavation and track-widening near the lake. Bhat had asked glaciologist and Islamic University of Science and Technology (IUST) Vice-Chancellor Prof Shakil Ahmad Romshoo, J&K Pollution Control Committee chairman Vasu Yadav and Chief Wildlife Warden Sarvesh Rai to examine the works, particularly their potential impact on the lake, glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) risks and surrounding alpine habitats. Singh also called on Environment and Forest Minister Altaf Ahmad Kaloo to facilitate a joint briefing by the experts.
